claims.text: The as-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase, primarily FCC solid solution.
Removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alters the stacking-fault energy of FeNiCrMn.
FeNiCrMn undergoes a temperature- and strain-rate-dependent transition between dislocation-mediated plasticity and deformation twinning.
Intermediate temperatures and moderate strain rates activate deformation twinning in FeNiCrMn.
Impeded dislocation glide increases work hardening and delays necking.
Twin-mediated work hardening maintains high strength together with ductility in the proposed intermediate regime.
At very low or very high strain rates, or at extreme temperatures, deformation is dominated by dislocation slip with little significant twinning.
The proposed intermediate regime will produce greater twin density than a dislocation-slip-dominated baseline.
The proposed intermediate regime will produce a higher work-hardening rate than a dislocation-slip-dominated baseline.
The proposed intermediate regime will produce higher yield strength at comparable ductility than the baseline.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi has a less pronounced twinning response than Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The strength–ductility balance of Co-free FeNiCrMn is uniquely improved by deformation-twin activation relative to the Co-containing counterpart.
The proposed mechanism applies from approximately 77 K to 500 K and from 10^-4 to 10^0 s^-1 in the as-solidified single-phase FCC state.
Outside the stated temperature and strain-rate ranges, grain-boundary sliding or creep may dominate and the twinning effect may cease to operate.
